documents.text: ₹2,659 crore lender financing, ₹2,133 crore equity/related contribution and ₹1,746 crore VGF for ₹6,538 crore project. Company disclosure, not bank drawdown ledger. Consortium members not named. Retained evidence: irb-financial-closure.body, irb-financial-closure.receipt.json

documents.title: IRB: equity raise and project-manager consideration
documents.text: First equity raise reported complete; separate contractual EPC and lifetime O&M consideration to IRB. ₹5,279 crore EPC and ₹5,180 crore O&M are contractual consideration plus taxes over different periods, not payments already received. GIC affiliate is generic in this release. Retained evidence: irb-gic-investment.body, irb-gic-investment.receipt.json

documents.title: IRB Trust: MBEL acquisition approval and related-party terms
documents.text: MBEL 51% IRB/49% Anahera; unitholders approved related-party transaction on 6 February 2024; issuer says arm’s length. Arm’s-length language is an issuer assertion. Approval is distinct from closing and independent valuation fairness. Retained evidence: source-04.body, source-04.receipt.json

documents.title: IRB Trust: Ganga Group I toll collection commenced
documents.text: MBEL commenced toll collection effective 17 May 2026, after provisional certificate/trial operations. Retained evidence: irb-toll-start.body, irb-toll-start.receipt.json

documents.title: JICA: C4 construction milestone and executing agency
documents.text: Lender confirms L&T/NHSRCL C4 agreement 26 Nov 2020 and whole-project loan support. Retained evidence: jica-c 4.body, jica-c 4.receipt.json

documents.title: JICA: MAHSR tranche 5 signed with Government of India
documents.text: JPY 400 bn tranche 5; cumulative JPY 1,050 bn project commitment. NHSRCL executing agency. Commitment, not expenditure; cumulative figure already includes tranche 5. Loan is to Government of India for whole project, not direct corporate borrowing by L&T. Retained evidence: source-11.body, source-11.receipt.json

documents.title: MEIL company memorandum in official EGM notice
documents.text: Exact corporate legal name corroborates CAG’s named contractor. Historic memorandum subscriber names are not treated as current shareholders. No name-only tender-corpus merge. Retained evidence: meil-legal.body, meil-legal.receipt.json

documents.title: NHIDCL current project-status register: Zojila
documents.text: Authority names MEIL for exact Zojila project and records ongoing status. Website current-status table is mutable and not a payment ledger. Financial-cost/current-schedule cells need header-aware reconciliation before interpreting variations. Retained evidence: source-13.body, source-13.receipt.json

documents.title: NHSRCL official awarded-tender register: first displayed 20 rows
documents.text: C4 awarded to Larsen & Toubro with separate INR, JPY and USD components. Direct original fetch returned HTTP 503; retained full Exa-indexed official page text is the content evidence. This page slice is not the complete tender population. Retained evidence: fetch-nhsrcl.json, nhsrcl-register-20 rows.json, nhsrcl-awards.receipt.json

documents.title: NHSRCL: C4 contract agreement signing
documents.text: L&T signed 237 km civil package; technical bids 23 Sep, financial bids 19 Oct, LOA 28 Oct 2020. Direct host 503; indexed official content retained. Scheduled duration is not completion certification. Retained evidence: fetch-nhsrcl.json, source-09.receipt.json

documents.title: NHSRCL: public ownership and JICA financing terms
documents.text: Government of India 50%, Gujarat 25%, Maharashtra 25%; described project loan terms. Authorized capital is not equity paid in. These historical participation ratios are not inferred payment amounts. Direct host 503. Retained evidence: fetch-updates.json, nhsrcl-ownership.receipt.json

documents.title: NHSRCL: account of C4 award in 35 days
documents.text: Authority attributes speed to parallel multidisciplinary coordination and consultant support. Agency account of its own process, not an independent compliance audit. This is independently dated award chronology, not the tender-corpus comparison field. Retained evidence: fetch-nhsrcl.json, source-10.receipt.json

documents.title: Lok Sabha question 3007: funding for Polavaram Phase I
documents.text: Central Phase I grant excludes powerhouse; powerhouse cost borne by Andhra Pradesh. Main-dam/LA/R&R milestone target June 2027. Does not adjudicate or settle CAG’s separate material-advance/equipment findings. Grant releases to project are not traced to MEIL bills. Retained evidence: polavaram-answer-2026.body, polavaram-answer-2026.receipt.json

documents.title: CAG Report 19 of 2023: Bharatmala Phase I
documents.text: Audit questions project prioritisation, appraisal, elevated design justification and execution. Includes Mo RTH replies and auditor rejoinders. The ₹18.20 crore/km programme norm and ₹250.77 crore/km sanctioned urban expressway civil cost have different scope; their ratio is not a measured like-for-like overrun. Primary-host indexed text was read; original PDF retrieval returned HTTP 503. Layout repetition/truncation limits downstream extraction. Publication day corroborated by contemporaneous report; audit period predates much of the publication window. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: NHAI report on Meachi bridge foundation settlement, NH 327 E
documents.text: At chainage 24+461 on the Galgalia–Bahadurganj section, the bridge under construction experienced about 600 mm pile-foundation settlement; the preliminary inquiry considered constricted river flow and scour. Preliminary causal explanation and temporary personnel suspensions do not establish final liability. Release names GR Infra Projects Highway Ltd and project concessionaire GR Galgalia Bahadurganj Highway Private Limited distinctly; parent ownership is not inferred. No final inquiry report or contractor reply retrieved. Galgalia and Bahadurganj name corridor endpoints; the exact bridge at chainage 24+461 is not assigned to either locality without geolocation. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: NHAI action after Cherkkala slope-protection collapse
documents.text: NHAI attributes slope collapse to design, protection and drainage deficiencies, announces debarment and a show-cause notice for one year/up to ₹9 crore, and says reconstruction is at concessionaire cost. Show-cause proposed duration/maximum penalty is not a verified final penalty or present-day debarment status. No contractor response or final expert committee report was located in this source set. HAM 15-year maintenance and own-cost reconstruction mean repair does not establish a second public payment. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: Guidelines on debarment of firms from bidding
documents.text: Guidelines separate ministry/entity debarment from cross-government debarment, require an opportunity to respond and preserve contracts concluded before an order. Debarment scope, commencement, expiry and allied-firm identity must be read from the actual order. A show-cause notice is not interchangeable with a final order. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: NHAI letter of award: Dwarka Expressway Package 4
documents.text: PIB identifies Larsen and Toubro as contractor for the Basai Ro B–NH 8/SPR package, 8.76 km, ₹1,047.007 crore, with two-year construction and four-year maintenance periods. Outside the five-year publication window; retained to resolve the historical contracting entity. Award announcement is not payment, completion certification or the total Dwarka project cost. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: Ministry official disputes Dwarka cost comparison
documents.text: A senior ministry official says elevated urban works are not comparable with the corridor norm and describes competitive bidding and appraisal. Official is unnamed in the article; this is a reported response, not a signed ministry order. The article’s aggregate estimate and per-km estimate do not form a clean internally consistent denominator; not used to calculate savings. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: NHAI preliminary report on under-construction Kerala VUP slab collapse
documents.text: Deck slab collapsed while concreting on Chengala–Neeleshwaram NH 66. NHAI’s preliminary explanation is scaffolding failure; an NIT expert committee was constituted. Headline says no injuries; body records one minor injury and no casualties. Body is retained. This VUP incident is a different asset and mechanism from the 2025 slope collapse on the same corridor. Preliminary cause is not a final inquiry finding. The August 2024 parliamentary annexure lists a Kerala NH 66 VUP staging failure at km 72+297 (PDF pp. 13–14) and reports suspensions/penalty; the 2022 release does not give chainage, so this is not automatically merged as the same asset. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/roads-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: Telangana State Finances Audit Report, year ended March 2022, Report 2 of 2023
documents.text: CAG traces ₹500 crore police-vehicle borrowing through TSPHCL, ₹328 crore budget-funded repayment by March 2022 and estimated ₹13 crore additional interest; separately examines police grant controls and Safe City budget utilisation. Report year is not a verified publication day; exact publication date remains unknown in this record. Budget, borrowing, repayment, and expenditure are distinct stages; these are dated audit observations, not a current fraud finding. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/state-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: CAG Karnataka Report No. 12 of 2025: implementation of Jal Jeevan Mission
documents.text: Section 3.3.1 records incomplete work in Hebbal, Shirahatti taluk, Gadag district during 2024 despite Har Ghar Jal reported status. Government responded in May 2025 that the elevated reservoir was completed by 8 April 2025, with 200 m pipeline and 20 FHTCs remaining before certification/trial run. Section 3.5 discusses 33 tenders worth ₹251.75 crore invited/awarded after 31 March 2024; Government cites timely administrative approvals and delays from non-participation and re-tendering. Sections 3.7.1–3.7.2 identify missing cross-system project/contractor keys and 9,342 first-call single-bid awards among 38,231 finalised works, with government response. Report sample is 28 villages in seven districts; it is not a statewide failure rate. Har Ghar Jal reported status and certified status differ. Audit period begins before requested window; Hebbal implementation findings from 2024 and response from 2025 are separately dated. No evidence of current 2026 conditions or individual guilt is inferred. Exact original publication day unconfirmed; direct PDF retrieval returned HTTP 503. Section 3.5 distinguishes extended award deadlines: 15 March 2024 for in-village works and 31 March 2024 for multi-village schemes. The 33 flagged tenders were after the later date; no universal 31 March deadline is inferred. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/services-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: Uttar Pradesh CAG 7/2025: DDUGJY and SAUBHAGYA
documents.text: Paragraph 3.3.4 attributes ₹46.27 crore paid for overlapping manpower/PMA work. The duplicate-connection headline is ₹26.65 crore; paragraphs 3.3.8–3.3.9 include grid and standalone-solar categories. Both responses and reported recovery progress accompany these historical findings. These are attributed audit conclusions, not criminal adjudications or current unrecovered loss. Audit period substantially predates the recent publication window. Chapter-only extraction lost body text; the full official report endpoint supplied readable indexed text. Original full-report binary returned HTTP 503; indexed primary text retained. Do not add the separately stated ₹4.41 crore standalone-solar duplicate category to the ₹26.65 crore headline: 3.3.8 listed amounts round to ₹22.24 crore, plus 3.3.9 ₹4.41 crore rounds to that headline. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/services-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: CAG landing record: UP electricity performance audit 7/2025
documents.text: Establishes the audit publication date and coverage through December 2022. Tabling date is not the date of the expenditure or government reply. Reused existing evidence from research/raw/public-works/services-research.json; not a fresh discovery or fresh primary retrieval.

documents.title: UPEIDA: four Ganga Expressway selected bidders and lowest-grant bids
documents.text: IRB selected for Group I; Adani Enterprises for Groups II–IV. Criterion is lowest public grant, not lowest total project cost. Retained evidence: source-01.body, source-01.receipt.json

documents.title: CPPP original notice 2020_NHIDC_564017_1
documents.text: Original notice fields accessible, estimate ₹4,429.83 crore; exact corpus-ID query returns 0. Notice estimate is not award/payment. Zero exact-ID corpus hits does not establish absence of the contract. Retained evidence: source-14.body, source-14.receipt.json, zojila-exact-query.json

documents.title: The Akshaya Patra Foundation Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Contains audited trust financial statements signed 7 October 2025, programme narrative, a Chikkajala kitchen table and note 2.25 related-party disclosures. Financial-statement audit does not independently verify all meal counts, nutrition or learning outcomes in the narrative. The auditor gives an unmodified opinion with emphasis on the trust’s adopted accounting basis. Support from state governments combines programme types and accounting components; organisation-wide support is not a Chikkajala-only grant. The scanned tables require visual verification; OCR is retained as a finding aid and is not authoritative.

documents.title: Akshaya Patra’s Chikkajala kitchen inauguration
documents.text: Names the Thakkar Family Foundation as patron donor and states the kitchen’s planned reach in Yelahanka, Jakkur and Hebbal. Inauguration capacity and planned reach are not meals actually served. Dignitary attendance is not evidence of a grant, corporate donor or improper influence.

documents.title: Byju Raveendran v GLAS Trust: procedural appeal dismissed
documents.text: Appeal against an order merely listing the application was held non-maintainable. The parties’ underlying creditor-claim disputes were left open. Direct mirror retrieval returned HTTP 403; indexed primary text archived in svcFetch 2.json, with irrelevant residential-address lines omitted. No later merits order is established. This is not a ruling that every GLAS claim or alleged transfer was valid.

documents.title: GLAS Trust Company LLC v BYJU Raveendran: 2024 INSC 811
documents.text: Primary judgment separates the US credit facility, Indian guarantee, settlement objections and the statutory insolvency-withdrawal procedure. ₹158 crore was ordered held by the committee of creditors in escrow. Paragraphs 86–87 expressly decline merits adjudication and any finding on stakeholder conduct. Recited allegations about US transfers are not treated as findings of this Indian judgment.

documents.title: Khyati directors’ discharge applications refused after rehearing
documents.text: Reports that the trial court heard the discharge pleas following a High Court direction and again refused discharge. Original discharge and remand orders not retrieved. Latest retained trial-stage observation is May 2026; no final conviction or acquittal is established by this corpus.

documents.title: Gujarat High Court: Prashant Vazirani v State of Gujarat, regular bail
documents.text: Records the clinical defence, State allegations and expert-review material considered at bail. Later bail developments are separately retained. Direct mirror retrieval returned HTTP 403; indexed court text is archived in svcFetch 1.json and svcFetch 4.json. A bail order uses a prima facie standard; it is not a conviction. Patient names are not entities in the structured slice.

documents.title: Khyati chairman bail hearing: reported PM-JAY earnings and bank-loan use
documents.text: Reports prosecution submissions and the sessions bail order, including the chairman’s denial of personal withdrawal and day-to-day involvement. The underlying bank ledger and sessions order were not independently retrieved. Earnings in a reported order are not verified bank receipts or adjudicated illicit proceeds.

documents.title: Khyati supplementary charge sheet names hospital holding company
documents.text: Identifies the company behind Khyati Multispeciality Hospital and reports the Ahmedabad Detection of Crime Branch charge sheet. Charge sheet filing is a prosecution step. The article is not a company-register extract or final criminal judgment.

documents.title: Supreme Court grants Kartik Jasubhai Patel bail
documents.text: Supreme Court allowed the petition and directed release on bail after noting bail granted to the co-accused. This supersedes the earlier custody snapshot. Direct mirror retrieval returned HTTP 403; indexed primary order archived in svcFetch 2.json. Bail is neither acquittal nor a finding that the allegation was false.

documents.title: CAG Report 10 of 2023: NSAP publicity expenditure
documents.text: Traces approved publicity heads, work orders to DAVP, actual NSAP IEC charge and lack of work-execution confirmation. Direct original PDF again returned HTTP 503 on 7 October 2026. Existing indexed original text, retrieved 6 October 2026, is archived with its provenance. The Ministry’s statement that it referred the issue internally is a response, not evidence of completed recovery.

documents.title: Lok Sabha Standing Committee 31 st report: NSAP action taken
documents.text: Checked later parliamentary scrutiny of NSAP. The report concerns scheme recommendations and does not establish settlement of CAG §5.5.1’s 2017 DAVP transactions. A later action-taken report on another committee report is not automatically an action-taken note closing this CAG paragraph. Non-observation in this document does not prove no remediation happened elsewhere.

documents.title: Rajya Sabha reply: measures to prevent misuse of AB-PMJAY
documents.text: Documents the ministry’s national anti-fraud and audit mechanism; not a Khyati-specific recovery order. National disciplinary totals cannot be attributed to a named hospital without a hospital-specific order.

documents.title: AISHE Report 2023-24
documents.text: 48,246 colleges were registered and 46,468 responded. Of responding colleges, 17.1% were government, 12.9% private aided and 70.0% private unaided. Contains state tables for private/government colleges and district distribution. Responding-college percentages must not be applied as exact counts to all registered colleges. Institution prevalence is not a funding share.

documents.title: Union Ministry releases AISHE 2022-23 and 2023-24 reports
documents.text: For 2023-24, 59,533 of 64,756 registered HEIs participated. Higher education enrolment is reported as 4.50 crore in 2023-24. GER is 30 in 2023-24 and uses ages 18-23 population projections based on Census 2011. Participation is voluntary and data is self-reported by institutions. Registration, survey response and estimated enrolment have different denominators. Report reference period differs from publication date.

documents.title: AISHE Final Reports
documents.text: Lists 2023-24 and 2022-23 final reports and Excel files. Index page is a discovery source, not a transaction or district funding ledger.

documents.title: Akshaya Patra Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Foundation describes PM POSHAN implementation for government/government-aided schools. Report says FY 2024–25 operations cover 16 states and 3 UTs. Government contributions are reported as ₹42,093.64 lakh and total income ₹85,746.61 lakh. New kitchens include Bengaluru locations, Pilerne in Goa and Kanpur. Government contributions include Anganwadi nutrition; not all school funding. Government contribution is within total income; avoid double counting. Kitchen city coverage is not equivalent to school-recipient district or a grant amount. States/cities arrays are documented examples, not full footprint.

documents.title: Azim Premji University Bengaluru Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Report identifies the university as not-for-profit, private and established under a Karnataka Act. Azim Premji Foundation is named sponsoring body. Report provides institutional teaching and research context. No university donation or scholarship amount validated in this extraction. Private university status does not imply eligibility for private equity distribution. Do not generalize one institution's funding arrangements to all private colleges.

documents.title: Five years, 10 states: Where India's government school count fell the most
documents.text: Reports uneven state-level net school-count reductions and warns against reading stock differences as a simple linear demographic story. Secondary lead, not proof of individual closures or wrongdoing. Do not import the headline as a closure-event count.

documents.title: Educate Girls FCRA financial statements for year ended 31 March 2024
documents.text: Document is financial statements prepared under FCRA for foreign contribution received and utilised. Income statement reports ₹1,08,44,95,261 donations for year ended 31 March 2024, separately from other income. Statements are signed 16 December 2024. PDF table extraction is fragmented; manually verify layout before treating each expense line as structured. Organisation-wide foreign donations do not establish donor-by-city or school-level funding. Upload path 2026 is not the fiscal year or signature date.

documents.title: Educate Girls Annual Progress Report FY 2024–25
documents.text: Audacious Project narrative identifies Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar expansion geography. FY 2024–25 report self-reports 285,237 girls enrolled through Vidya. Report describes two temporary learning centres in Prayagraj during Maha Kumbh for migrant workers' children. Programme outcomes are organisation-reported. No city-level monetary allocation established. The four named states describe a particular initiative, not necessarily the full NGO footprint. Annual programme reach cannot be summed with individual-school enrolment without deduplication.

documents.title: FCRA Online Services dashboard
documents.text: Dashboard distinguishes active/alive association count from annual returns filed across active, expired, cancelled and deemed ceased associations. State breakdown is explicitly for all association types. Registry counts are not education NGO counts or funding amounts. Snapshot may lag and uses legacy place names. Association address is not beneficiary location; do not map receipts to headquarters as local school funding.

documents.title: FCRA Online Services: Annual Returns (FC-4)
documents.text: Official portal provides FC-4 annual return filing guidance, sample form and document requirements. Portal landing page proves reporting route, not receipt by a particular school. FCRA registration or prior permission is not evidence of donation receipt or programme deployment. Sample-form fetch returned no extracted page content.

documents.title: HDFC Bank Parivartan CSR Report FY 2024–25
documents.text: CSR education work includes remedial learning, teacher training, scholarships and safe school infrastructure. ECSS supports continuation of education for economically vulnerable students. Projects implemented directly or through empanelled partners; disclosures also appear in directors' report and MCA filings. ₹1,068.03 crore report total covers all CSR sectors, not education alone; exclude from education totals. Report reach across 28 states/8 UTs refers to overall CSR, not proof of education spend in every jurisdiction. Current open scholarship applications or eligibility deadlines not verified here.

documents.title: 100 schools with zero enrolment denotified, 120 merged
documents.text: Reports 100 zero-enrolment primary/middle schools denotified and 120 primary schools with five or fewer students merged. Reports difficult-terrain and tribal-area schools were exempted from merger. Original school-wise notifications not obtained. Counts refer to different administrative actions and should remain separate. Zero enrolment and low enrolment are the official rationale reported; no matched catchment population evidence establishes a contradiction.

documents.title: Government urged to withdraw order allowing merger of low-enrolment schools
documents.text: Reports minister's statement that government has no plans to shut any government school. Reports AIDSO seeking withdrawal of a merger clause and a written assurance. Capture minister's denial alongside access concerns. School closure, transfer of classes and administrative merger may refer to different units. No inference of dishonesty or wrongdoing.

documents.title: Karnataka rolls out project to merge government schools with KPS magnet schools
documents.text: Reports a seven-school pilot linked to Honganuru KPS. Quotes circular instructions on student transfers and transport arrangements. Reports concern from educationists/student organisations about rural access. Underlying circular not retrieved in this pass. Announced/proposed state scale is not completed implementation. Allegation that a much larger number of schools would close is not adopted as a fact.

documents.title: KKR and PSP invest in Lighthouse Learning
documents.text: KKR funds invest alongside new investor PSP; KKR continues to hold a majority stake. Recipient described as an education services provider/platform. Release names presence in Bangalore, Mumbai, Pune, Hyderabad and Delhi-NCR. No transaction amount disclosed in the primary announcement. Do not substitute media transaction estimates as primary-verified values. Equity in services platform is distinct from donations to schools, ownership of regulated educational trusts, or FCRA contributions. Presence is not proof investment proceeds were spent in every named city; Delhi NCR crosses administrative borders. Delhi-NCR presence is a regional label; it does not establish a school or spending location within Delhi's administrative boundary.

documents.title: Closure of Government Schools — Lok Sabha Unstarred Question 1374
documents.text: Annexure I reports government-school stock counts for five academic years by state/UT. Annexure II reports government-school stock counts for all Uttar Pradesh districts. India government schools: 1,022,386 in 2021-22 and 1,005,245 in 2025-26. NEP paragraph 7.4 says consolidation should only proceed when access is unaffected. The answer provides stock counts, not a school-by-school closure or merger register. Districts are not cities or school catchments. No matched population series or causal impact evaluation is provided. Reported by states/UTs through UDISE+.

documents.title: Declining Enrolment of Students in Government Schools in Uttar Pradesh — Lok Sabha Question 2445
documents.text: Provides approved central and actual released central shares for Uttar Pradesh Samagra Shiksha and PM SHRI for three financial years. Shamli district government-school counts rise from 621 in 2021-22 to 623 in 2025-26. The requested district spending is answered with state-level approved/released figures; do not label these district spending. Releases are not expenditure, audited utilisation, or money received by an individual school. Annexures contain government-school counts, not verified closure events.

documents.title: National CSR Portal: company-wise project disclosures
documents.text: Schema includes project, sector, state, district, amount outlay in INR crore, amount spent in INR crore and implementation mode. Portal says company board/director reports take precedence if inconsistent. PAN India includes multiple-state projects and centralized funds. Captcha and dynamic selection prevent treating landing page as a project extract. Company registered office must not be substituted for project location. Preserve PAN India and NEC/Not Mentioned instead of distributing across states. No recipient-level totals verified.

documents.title: MCA Corporate Data Management: CSR Data
documents.text: Portal provides year, state, PSU/non-PSU and development sector filters and an implementing agency master. Displayed education sector is combined with differently abled and livelihood categories. Dynamic data values were not extracted. Do not label grouped-sector expenditure as education-only spending. Heading and filter years differ; verify downloaded report timestamp before publishing totals.

documents.title: Cabinet approves MERITE with ₹4,200 crore outlay
documents.text: Scheme targets 175 engineering institutions and 100 polytechnics. Total financial implication is ₹4,200 crore, including ₹2,100 crore World Bank loan assistance. Government/government-aided technical institutions are expected to be selected. National eligibility is not proof every city or state has an awarded institution. Targets are planned benefits, not realized outcomes. World Bank share is part of total and must not be added again.

documents.title: Cabinet approves PM SHRI Schools
documents.text: Total project cost ₹27,360 crore, including central share ₹18,128 crore, over five years. Targets more than 14,500 existing schools managed by central/state/UT/local government. Selection uses eligibility checks and challenge mode. Multi-year programme outlay is not current-year expenditure or total India education funding. Not a grant programme for all private unaided schools. National targets do not verify city-level awards.

documents.title: PM Schools for Rising India — scheme information
documents.text: At the page's update, 12,079 schools had been selected through four phases. Confirms ₹27,360 crore total and ₹18,128 crore central project cost. Selection snapshot is dated November 2024 and must not be labelled current in October 2026.

documents.title: PM-USHA: Building Stronger Institutions for a Knowledge-Driven Future
documents.text: Scheme outlay ₹12,926.10 crore for 2023-24 to 2025-26. First two PAB meetings approved 440 units worth ₹5,613.12 crore. FY 2025-26 budget stated as ₹1,815 crore. Eight new model degree college units approved across Nagaland (4), Manipur (2), Meghalaya (2), totaling ₹119.98 crore. Outlay, PAB approvals and annual budget are distinct stages and cannot be added together. A unit is not necessarily a unique institution. Snapshot is May 2025; not live allocations.

documents.title: PM-USHA Guidelines
documents.text: Covers government and government-aided higher education institutions of states/UTs. Gives priority to focus districts and defines components and eligibility. Eligibility and programme scope do not establish that an institution has received funding. Historical AISHE figures in the guidelines are not current counts.

documents.title: Population Projections for India and States 2011–2036
documents.text: Uses Census 2011, SRS fertility/mortality and migration assumptions. Projects total population increase and a decline in the national population aged 5–14 during 2011–2036. Projections are model-based rather than new census observations. Total population growth cannot substitute for school-age population growth. District/city downscaling requires separate validation. Mirrored copies surfaced differing summary totals; numeric population claims are intentionally omitted until document edition provenance is reconciled.

documents.title: Pratham Education Foundation Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Report describes direct learning programmes and district, city and state government partnerships. Report contains financials and supporters sections. Historical Mumbai municipal-school partnerships are documented. Self-reported programme reach is not a school funding receipt. Historical Mumbai narrative does not prove current city funding allocation. No financial totals from this report validated; full financial section not extracted in this pass.

documents.title: Quota for EWS Seats in Private Unaided Schools — Lok Sabha Question 1260
documents.text: Provides sanctioned and reimbursed-to-school amounts under RTE for Karnataka for five years. FY 2025-26 sanctioned ₹156.10 crore and reimbursed ₹148.68 crore. Government says reimbursement is timely, based on information from the state. Describes 2018 Karnataka neighbourhood-school exemption. Including Bengaluru does not make this city-level funding. The table covers the reimbursement claim population; do not interpret as uniquely new entry-grade admissions without checking definitions. Sanctioned less reimbursed does not establish overdue obligations or misuse. Distinct from central releases to the state; do not sum with Samagra central share as independent money.

documents.title: Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009
documents.text: Section 12(1)(c) provides entry-level admissions for eligible disadvantaged/weaker-section children of at least 25% in specified categories of schools. Section 12(2) provides private unaided school reimbursement capped at state per-child expenditure or actual charge, whichever is lower, with provisos for pre-existing free-education obligations. Not an unrestricted private-school capital grant. School eligibility, constitutional/applicability exclusions, neighbourhood rules and claims are determined by applicable law and state implementation. Statutory eligibility is not evidence of payment.

documents.title: Chhattisgarh Samagra Shiksha 2025-26 revised PAB minutes
documents.text: Approved annual work plan: ₹232,029.17 lakh including ₹82,492.13 lakh spillover. Planned central share to be released: ₹112,900.28 lakh; corresponding state share ₹75,267.52 lakh. Supplementary ICT labs and smart classrooms approval: ₹14,133.80 lakh. Supersedes sections of earlier 9 May 2025 minutes; preserve version history. The section heading says Actual Release, but the line explicitly says to be released: classify as planned/approved, not actual disbursement. Opening balances and spillover make the approved plan different from fresh allocations. OCR affects table layout; use explicit prose figures and reconcile original PDF before bulk extraction. Origin PDF returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-06; preserve indexed-text access status and locate replacement archive before treating as live-verified.

documents.title: Documents & Reports — Samagra Shiksha PAB minutes
documents.text: Provides state/UT financial-year entries with minutes, supplementary minutes, addenda and revisions. An index to retrieve further records, not extracted transaction coverage. Document links may move; origin link health must be checked. Index includes organisations as well as states, so row count is not geographic coverage.

documents.title: Tata Trusts Annual Report 2024–25
documents.text: Grant disbursal table reports ₹247.47 crore education institutional/direct implementation spend and ₹40.91 crore education individual grants. Report explicitly distinguishes institutional grants from individual grants. No city/state allocation derived from aggregate table. Institutional/direct implementation spend is broader than unrestricted school grants. These amounts should not be combined with NGO recipient disclosures without donor-recipient deduplication.

documents.title: Ministry of Education releases UDISE+ 2024-25 report
documents.text: Reports 104,125 single-teacher schools and 7,993 zero-enrolment schools in 2024-25. Reports total teachers 10,122,420. Reports computer access in 64.7% and internet in 63.5% of schools. National aggregate with mixed management categories; not a city-level finding. A zero-enrolment school is not necessarily a closed school. 2025-26 official parliamentary school-count data is newer.

documents.title: Report on UDISE+ 2023-24 — existing structure
documents.text: Separates government, government-aided, private unaided recognised, and other schools. Reports that student-wise collection from 2022-23 is not strictly comparable with earlier aggregate reporting for several education indicators. Historical methodology reference; not latest school data. Population denominator moderation can affect ratio comparisons. UDISE listing alone does not confer recognition.

documents.title: UP govt tells HC: No merger if school has over 50 students, 1km distance
documents.text: Reports extension of interim status quo for school pairing in Sitapur until 1 September 2025. Reports government assurances on enrolment/distance and court clarification that interim order does not affect overall policy. Historical interim procedural status, not current case disposition. Later court orders must be obtained before stating present legality or operative stay.

documents.title: Krishna Kumari and others v State of UP — 2025:AHC-LKO:38113
documents.text: Paragraph 3 identifies Government Order 16 June 2025 and consequent 24 June 2025 list of 105 schools challenged in petitions. Exa extract reviewed through early statutory discussion; final disposition not independently extracted. Subsequent appeal reporting exists; do not present this as final current case status.

documents.title: No merger for schools with 50 or more students as Uttar Pradesh government revises plan
documents.text: Reports minister's clarification excluding schools with 50 or more students and schools farther than 1km from pairing. Reports minister saying UDISE codes remain unchanged, buildings may host Bal Vatikas, and original classes can resume if enrolment/capacity warrants. Reported policy and explanation, not independent verification of implementation. Do not turn nearly 10,000 proposed pairings into confirmed permanent closures. Preserved codes mean stock series can miss changes in where teaching takes place.

documents.title: World Bank approves STARS to improve India's education system
documents.text: World Bank approved a USD 500 million STARS programme. Programme supports quality and governance of school education in six named states. Loan maturity 17.5 years including five-year grace period. Approval is not disbursement or per-state allocation. Source page extraction metadata says 2021-01-29 but article dateline is June 24, 2020; use dateline. Countrywide beneficiaries and six-state activities must not be treated as identical scope.

documents.title: STARS implementation status and results report, ISR59758
documents.text: Report states cumulative disbursement of USD 196.75 million (39.35%) against the USD 500 million programme. Report discusses programme restructuring and a requested extension. Historical snapshot, not current 2026 disbursement. Do not add disbursement to original loan value. A request for extension is not proof that an extension was approved.

documents.title: Adani Power annual report FY2022-23, filed 27 June 2023
documents.text: Reports Essar Power MP acquisition/control on 16 March 2022, rename to Mahan Energen, ₹1 crore equity infusion and ₹600 crore upfront lender payment; locates 1,200MW plant in Singrauli. Issuer disclosure, not an independent assessment of acquisition fairness. ₹1 crore equity, ₹600 crore upfront and ₹2,500 crore plan-realizable figure are different stages and must not be summed as separate awards.

documents.title: IBBI summary of Supreme Court Essar Steel judgment
documents.text: Official regulator summary explains Supreme Court reversal of the July 2019 NCLAT approach and treatment of resolution claims. Summary is not the full Supreme Court judgment. Historical legal context; not proof of later execution or current balances.

documents.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy News, April–June 2026
documents.text: 1,484 resolution plans; ₹435,469.89 crore creditor realization measure against ₹1,426,665.38 crore admitted claims; methodology and fair-value denominator caveats. Snapshot is 30 June 2026; exact issue-publication date not established. Table labels use realizable value while surrounding text uses realized. It is not independently verified cash collected by the snapshot. Fair-value ratio covers 1,359 cases, not all 1,484.

documents.title: Corporate insolvency resolutions as at 30 September 2022
documents.text: Named debtor CINs, admitted financial/operational claims and realizable amounts under approved plans. Data supplied by resolution professionals. Amounts are realizable, not NPV and not verified cash recovery. 2022 snapshot cannot settle subsequent implementation, appeals or guarantee recoveries.

documents.title: PM CARES current About page and account index
documents.text: Six statements through FY2024-25 are now linked. Ex officio PM chair and Defence, Home and Finance ministers; current nominated trustees K. T. Thomas and Kariya Munda. Webpage update is not the publication date of each PDF. A self-description of legal status is not a court determination.

documents.title: PM CARES registered trust deed
documents.text: Deed recites non-governmental character while assigning ex officio trusteeship and PMO administrative support. Earlier than the five-year recent-record window; constitutional background. The trust recital does not decide the statutory public-authority test.

documents.title: PM CARES current FAQs
documents.text: PMO honorary administration, contribution eligibility, current auditor KKC appointed for three years and FCRA position. Appointment start date and FCRA exemption instrument are not supplied by these passages.

documents.title: PM CARES audited Receipts and Payments FY2023-24
documents.text: Original scan signed by KKC partner Tejas Parikh on 7 August 2026; net domestic donations, interest, refunds, payments and balances. Audit signature date is known; publication date is not. Notes 1–16 and the separate referenced audit report are absent from this linked PDF.

documents.title: PM CARES audited Receipts and Payments FY2024-25
documents.text: Original scan separates domestic and foreign donations net of refunds, savings and FD interest, TDS refund and implementing-agency refunds. Cash account does not identify donors, implementing agencies or final recipients. Signature 7 August 2026 is not a publication date.

documents.title: Centre for Public Interest Litigation v Union of India, WP(C)546/2020
documents.text: Court refused a direction requiring transfer of PM CARES funds to NDRF and discussed the charitable trust audit context. The judgment does not adjudicate RTI section 2(h). Pre-window legal background, not a current case-status determination.

documents.title: PMNRF current accounts index
documents.text: Current original page links audited FY2023-24 and FY2024-25 accounts; both were downloaded. Comparator supplies context, not a causal or intent test.

documents.title: Framework for Compromise Settlements and Technical Write-offs
documents.text: Technical write-off preserves borrower claims; compromise can waive claims to an agreed extent. Sets policy, approval, reporting and cooling-period rules. Historical circular; current commercial-bank provisions are read from the 2025 Directions as updated 1 October 2026.

documents.title: Commercial Banks – Resolution of Stressed Assets Directions, 2025, updated 1 October 2026
documents.text: Defines compromise and technical write-off separately; board governance, criminal-proceedings preservation and continued penal measures for wilful default/fraud. Commercial-bank applicability; do not substitute similarly titled rural cooperative-bank directions. The current consolidation includes amendments; original issue date alone does not identify the operative version.

documents.title: Lok Sabha Q120: Waiver of loans
documents.text: PSB Large–Industries & Services domestic write-offs and actual recoveries; all-borrower ≥₹100 crore write-off count; confidentiality and mixed-vintage recovery caveats. FY2025-26 figures provisional. Corporate-loan category not separately collected. Annual recoveries are not a cohort recovery rate; all-type CRILC count is not a corporate or billionaire list.

documents.title: SEBI final order: Adicorp transactions — 31671/2025-26
documents.text: SEBI found the specified show-cause allegations unestablished under the rules applicable to the transactions and disposed of proceedings without directions. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked. A final regulatory decision on specified noticees/transactions, not a criminal acquittal or clearance of every allegation involving a corporate group. Original cover identities reviewed; personal tax identifiers excluded from the retained excerpts.

documents.title: Parliament reply: proceedings based on CAG findings — Lok Sabha Q.2191

Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked. The answer reports a CBI case, not a complete census of all state or agency actions on CAG reports. Filing a closure report does not establish court acceptance. The underlying case file and closure order were not retrieved.

documents.title: Electoral bonds constitutional judgment — 2024 INSC 113

Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: PM CARES / NDRF fund-transfer judgment — W.P.(C) 546/2020
documents.text: Historical judgment refuses compulsory transfer of PM CARES funds to NDRF and distinguishes their legal/audit regimes. It is not a transaction-level audit or an RTI-status determination. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked. Historical background, outside the 6 October 2021–6 October 2026 recent window. Does not establish current financial balances, donor identities, procurement delivery or general RTI status.

documents.title: SBI disclosure extension refused — 2024 INSC 195
documents.text: SBI sought time until 30 June 2024. The Court required disclosure by 12 March and ECI publication by 15 March; contempt jurisdiction was not exercised at that stage. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: Sita Soren legislative-immunity reference — 2024 INSC 161
documents.text: The seven-judge bench held legislative speech/vote immunity does not immunise bribery prosecution. The reference answers the constitutional question, not individual criminal guilt. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: SWAMIH / Gayatri Aura information dispute — Delhi HC W.P.(C) 4353/2025
documents.text: The Court declined the RTI petition on forum/territorial grounds with liberty to approach the jurisdictional High Court; all rights and contentions remain open. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.text: No ground was shown to transfer SEBI investigations; the Court directed completion of two pending matters and expressly did not interfere with investigation outcomes. Only the issues and parties covered by this dated record are established. Later appeals, implementation and unrelated proceedings are not exhaustively tracked.

documents.title: Executed Delhi, Mumbai and security buyer-cohort scan
documents.text: Read-only scan of two rehashed original SQLite inputs and a fingerprint-verified derivation. Thirteen disjoint buyer-name probes keep notice/award rows, date eligibility, repeated keys and bid-count coverage separate. No money sum or corruption inference is produced. Notice and award listings are different grains. No notice-to-award join or payment trail is inferred. No prices are summed. Detail bidder labels are not resolved legal-company identities. Listing counts include historical, undated and date-invalid rows; dated eligible rows are reported separately. Repeated full buyer/portal/tender/reference keys are repeated source records, not evidence of repeated paid work. Single-bid observations require the original procurement method, qualification rules, corrigenda and award documents before any adverse conclusion. Zero matches under the declared buyer-name probe are a coverage gap, not proof that an institution has no tenders. No contact names, private addresses, bank details or tactical installation locations are extracted.

documents.text: Reported BMC RTI identifies Force One partners; separately reports Mashilkar/Vaze business association and Mashilkar’s no-contracts response. Original RTI annexures and company filings not obtained. Authored notes retain reported status. Reporter calls private-limited-company participants partners; no director title, share percentage, exact tenure or COVID money transfer inferred. Party roles are dated context, not evidence of a minister receiving money.

documents.title: Official SAFEMA appellate order: Suraj Satish Chavan, 13 July 2026
documents.text: Original attachment-appeal order supplies previously unretained bank-analysis summaries, two Sahyadri subcontract routes, exact Force One downstream values and the attachment disposition. Full official PDF retrieved and SHA 256 recorded. Repository retains a full text extract with bank-account numbers redacted; original is not published locally. Financial narratives reproduce investigation/account analysis; underlying bank statements and counterparty inward receipts were not independently obtained. An attachment-stage holding secures property pending trial; it is not a criminal conviction. Figures, typography and reasoning differ from prior bail record and contain unreconciled arithmetic.
